<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source URL pointing to a tagged release tarball from the official GitHub repository of dosbox-x. The `source` array entry uses HTTPS and refers to a predictable, versioned archive, which is consistent with normal AUR packaging practices. There are no command substitutions, process substitutions, or executable hooks in the global scope or within `pkgver()` — in fact, `pkgver()` is not defined at all, so the value is static.

The top-level content of the PKGBUILD consists only of variable assignments. No code is executed during sourcing that would trigger network activity, data exfiltration, or execution of external payloads. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, though even if it were 'SKIP', that alone would not make this unsafe for the current gate. Since `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` prevents execution of `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()`, any potentially dangerous operations inside those functions (which are not present anyway) would not be run at this stage.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD involves only safe operations: downloading a source tarball from a known upstream and parsing a clean, declarative PKGBUILD without active code injection or malicious side effects.
</details>
<evidence>

No active malicious code in sourcing or fetch phase
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The PKGBUILD is straightforward: it defines a standard source tarball from the official dosbox-x GitHub repository (`https://github.com/joncampbell123/dosbox-x/archive/dosbox-x-v${pkgver}.tar.gz`). There are no global-level commands that would execute during sourcing—only variable assignments and commented-out functions. The `pkgver` is a static string, not derived from external input. Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will simply download and extract the tarball; no malicious code can execute from the PKGBUILD itself at this stage. The `build()` and `package()` functions are not called under `--nobuild`. This file poses no immediate risk for the scoped commands.
</details>
